parts.name: overview
parts.prose: Guidelines for access control models and identity forwarding.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Secrets are injected at runtime

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: IA-5(7)
parts.prose: Runtime injection prevents static authenticators from being embedded in application code or container images

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Applications and workloads are explicitly authorized to communicate with each other using mutual authentication

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: IA-9
parts.prose: Mutual authentication between workloads establishes bidirectional identity verification before service communication

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Keys are rotated frequently

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-12
parts.prose: Key rotation is a key management lifecycle activity addressed by SC-12

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Key lifespan is short

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-12
parts.prose: Short key lifespan is a key management lifecycle policy addressed by SC-12

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Credentials and keys protecting sensitive workloads (health/finance/etc) are generated and managed independent of a cloud service provider

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: KMS and HMS are common technologies to achieve this. FIPS 140-2 compliance is strongly suggested. Cloud KMS tends to be FIPS 140-2 Level 2 or greater.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SA-9
parts.prose: Independent credential management addresses risk from reliance on external cloud provider services

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-12
parts.prose: Generation and management of credentials is a key management lifecycle activity

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Authentication and authorization are determined independently

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: IA-13
parts.prose: Independent authentication and authorization map to the separation of identity providers from authorization servers

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: AC-3
parts.prose: Authorization decisions are enforced as a distinct process from identity authentication

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Authentication and authorization are enforced independently

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: AC-3
parts.prose: Independent enforcement of authorization is distinct from the authentication mechanism that establishes identity

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Access control and file permissions are updated in real-time

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: where possible as caching may permit unauthorized access

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SI-4(2)
parts.prose: Real-time access control and permission updates require automated monitoring to detect and respond to changes

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Authorization for workloads is granted based on attributes and roles/permissions previously assigned

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: AC-3(13)
parts.prose: Workload authorization based on pre-assigned attributes aligns with attribute-based access control enforcement

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: AC-3(7)
parts.prose: Workload authorization based on pre-assigned roles and permissions aligns with role-based access control enforcement

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: ABAC and RBAC are used

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: AC-3(13)
parts.prose: ABAC enforces access decisions based on workload and environmental attributes

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: AC-3(7)
parts.prose: RBAC enforces access decisions based on pre-defined role assignments

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: End user identity is capable of being accepted, consumed, and forwarded on for contextual or dynamic authorization

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: This can be achieved through the use of identity documents and tokens.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: AC-24
parts.prose: Forwarded identity context enables dynamic authorization decisions at each service boundary

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All cluster and workloads operators are authenticated

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: IA-2
parts.prose: Cluster and workload operators are organizational users requiring unique identification and authentication

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Cluster and workloads operate actions are evaluated against access control policies governing context, purpose, and output

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: AC-3
parts.prose: Operator actions are evaluated against access control policies governing context, purpose, and output

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Identity federation uses multi-factor authentication

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: IA-2(1)
parts.prose: Identity federation requiring MFA applies to privileged account access

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: IA-2(2)
parts.prose: Identity federation requiring MFA applies to non-privileged account access

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: HSMs are used to physically protect cryptographic secrets with an encryption key residing in the HSM

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: If this is not possible, software-based credential managers should be used.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-12(1)
parts.prose: HSMs provide hardware-based key storage and management for cryptographic secret protection

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-3(1)
parts.prose: HSMs enforce hardware separation of cryptographic security functions from the general-purpose environment

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Secrets should have a short expiration period or time to live

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Leverage tool-specific capabilities of secret manager

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SI-12
parts.prose: Short expiration periods enforce timely disposal of secrets as a retention lifecycle policy

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Time to live and expiration period on secrets is verified to prevent reuse

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Leverage tool-specific capabilities of secret manager

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: IA-5
parts.prose: Verification of secret expiration and TTL prevents reuse of stale authenticators

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Secrets management systems are highly available

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-12(1)
parts.prose: Secrets management system availability ensures continuous access to cryptographic key infrastructure

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Long-lived secrets adhere to periodic rotation and revocation

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Long-lived secrets are not recommended, but some capabilities require them

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: IA-5
parts.prose: Periodic rotation and revocation of long-lived secrets is an authenticator management lifecycle activity

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Secrets are distributed through secured communication channels protected commensurate with the level of access or data they are protecting

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-8
parts.prose: Secrets distributed through communication channels require transmission confidentiality and integrity proportional to sensitivity

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Secrets injected at runtime are masked or dropped from logs, audit, or system dumps

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Even short lived secrets may be reused if caught in time by an interested attacker. Logs, audit, and systems dumps (i.e. in-memory shared volumes instead of environment variables) are all areas where runtime injected secrets show up

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: AU-9
parts.prose: Runtime secrets are masked or excluded to protect audit information from credential exposure

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Identity federation uses multi-factor authentication for human users

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: IA-2(1)
parts.prose: Identity federation with MFA requires multi-factor authentication for privileged users

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: IA-2(2)
parts.prose: Identity federation with MFA requires multi-factor authentication for non-privileged users

parts.name: overview
parts.prose: Guidelines for securing compute infrastructure including bootstrapping, isolation, monitoring, and runtime security.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Bootstrapping is employed to verify correct physical and logical location of compute

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Secure Boot with TPM 2.0 or similar control

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SI-7(9)
parts.prose: Bootstrapping verification of compute location is a boot process integrity check

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Disparate data sensitive workloads are not run on the same host OS kernel

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There are at least three implementing controls possible: workloads may be  separated by running in a separate cluster, on a separate node, or by implementing pods in independent VMs. It is also possible to emulate the kernel via an application kernel (e.g. gvisor)

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-39
parts.prose: Workloads with different data sensitivity classifications require separate kernel-level execution domains

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-7(21)
parts.prose: Isolation of workload components based on data sensitivity classification

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Monitor and detect any changes to the initial configurations made in runtime

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Preventative controls should be the primary control. Detective controls monitoring  filesystem changes should be used to verify primary controls are operating properly.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: CM-2(2)
parts.prose: Automated detection of runtime configuration drift from the established baseline

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: CM-3(7)
parts.prose: Runtime configuration changes are reviewed and correlated against authorized modifications

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: API auditing is enabled with a filter for a specific set of API Groups or verbs

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: API audits of the application, kubernetes API server, and kernel should be implemented.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: AU-2
parts.prose: Filtered API auditing defines the specific events and verbs captured for logging

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Container specific operating systems are in use

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A read-only OS with other services disabled. This provides isolation and resource confinement  that enables developers to run isolated applications on a shared host kernel

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: CM-2
parts.prose: Container-specific operating systems establish a purpose-built hardened baseline

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: CM-7
parts.prose: Container-specific operating systems remove unnecessary services and functionality by design

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The hardware root of trust is based in a Trusted Platform Module (TPM) or virtual TPM (vTPM)

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Ensure HW root of trust extends to the host OS kernel, modules, system images, container runtimes, and all software on

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SI-7
parts.prose: TPM and vTPM provide a hardware root of trust for software and firmware integrity verification

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Minimize administrative access to the control plane

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Ensure both users and pods have the minimum necessary access

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: AC-6
parts.prose: Minimizing administrative access to the control plane applies the principle of least privilege

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Object level and resource requests and limits are controlled through cgroups

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: helps prevent exhaustion of node and cluster level resources by one misbehaving workload due to an intentional (e.g., fork bomb attack or cryptocurrency mining) or unintentional (e.g., reading a large file in memory without input validation, horizontal autoscaling to exhaust compute resources) issue

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-6
parts.prose: Cgroup resource requests and limits enforce allocation boundaries to prevent resource exhaustion

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-39
parts.prose: Cgroups provide process-level isolation of resource consumption between workloads

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Systems processing alerts are periodically tuned for false positives

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: to avoid alert flooding, fatigue, and false negatives after security incidents that were not detected by the system

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SI-4(13)
parts.prose: Alert tuning for false positives refines traffic and event pattern analysis effectiveness

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All orchestrator control plane components are configured to communicate via mutual authentication and certificate validation with a periodically rotated certificate

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In unfederated clusters, the CA should be used exclusively for the current cluster.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: IA-9
parts.prose: Control plane components use mutual authentication and certificate validation to verify service identity

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-12
parts.prose: Periodic certificate rotation for control plane communication is a key management lifecycle activity

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Only sanctioned capabilities and system calls (e.g. seccomp filters), are allowed to execute or be invoked in a container by the host operating system

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Additional tooling should be installed that go beyond k8s capabilities to limit system calls. E.g. Falco.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: CM-2
parts.prose: Seccomp filters define a baseline of sanctioned system calls for container execution

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: CM-7
parts.prose: Restricting container capabilities and system calls enforces least functionality

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Changes to critical mount points and files are prevented, monitored, and alerted

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: CM-5
parts.prose: Protecting critical mount points and files from unauthorized modification is an access restriction for change

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Runtime configuration control prevents changes to binaries, certificates, and remote access configurations

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: CM-5
parts.prose: Runtime immutability of binaries, certificates, and remote access configurations restricts unauthorized change

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Runtime configuration prevents ingress and egress network access for containers to only what is required to operate

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-7
parts.prose: Container-level ingress and egress restrictions enforce network boundary protection at runtime

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Policies are defined that restrict communications to only occur between sanctioned microservice pairs

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-7
parts.prose: Microservice communication allow-listing is application-layer network segmentation

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Use a policy agent to control and enforce authorized, signed container images

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: CM-14
parts.prose: Policy agents enforcing image signatures validate that only signed components are admitted

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Use a policy agent to control provenance assurance for operational workloads

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SR-4(3)
parts.prose: Policy agents enforce provenance validation to confirm workload origin and integrity

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Use a service mesh that eliminates implicit trust through data-in-motion encryption (data in transit)

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-8
parts.prose: Service mesh encryption of data in transit protects transmission confidentiality and integrity

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Use components that detect, track, aggregate and report system calls and network traffic from a container

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: should be leveraged to look for unexpected or malicious behavior

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SI-4
parts.prose: Container-level observation of system calls and network traffic implements system monitoring

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Workloads should be dynamically scanned to detect malicious or insidious behavior for which no known occurrence yet exists

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Events such as an extended sleep command that executes data exfiltration from etcd after the workload has been running for X amount of days are not expected in the majority of environments and therefore are not included in security tests. The aspect that workloads can have time or event delayed trojan horses is only detectable by comparing to baseline expected behavior, often discovered during thorough activity and scan monitoring

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SI-3
parts.prose: Dynamic behavioral scanning detects zero-day and previously unknown malicious activity in running workloads

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Environments are continuously scanned to detect new vulnerabilities in workloads

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Vulnerabilities are constantly being discovered, just because it wasn't vulnerable at deploy, doesn't mean it won't be vulnerable in two weeks

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: RA-5
parts.prose: Continuous environment scanning for workload vulnerabilities is a vulnerability monitoring activity

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Actionable audit events are generated that correlate/contextualize data from logs into "information" that can drive decision trees/incident response

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: AU-3
parts.prose: Sufficient audit record content is a prerequisite for log correlation and incident response decision-making

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Segregation of duties and the principle of least privilege is enforced

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: AC-6
parts.prose: Least privilege limits workload and operator permissions to the minimum required

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: AC-5
parts.prose: Segregation of duties prevents any single actor from controlling an entire critical function

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Non-compliant violations are detected based on a pre-configured set of rules defined by the organization's policies

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SI-7
parts.prose: Policy-based violation detection verifies system state integrity against organizational rules

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Native secret stores encrypt with keys from an external Key Management Store (KMS)

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-12
parts.prose: External KMS integration for native secret store encryption is a key management infrastructure decision

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Native secret stores are not configured for base64 encoding or stored in clear-text in the key-value store by default

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Encoding is not encryption

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-28(1)
parts.prose: Secret stores must use cryptographic protection rather than encoding for data at rest

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Network traffic to malicious domains is detected and denied

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SI-4
parts.prose: Detection and denial of traffic to malicious domains is network-level system monitoring

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Use encrypted containers for sensitive sources, methods, and data

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-28
parts.prose: Encrypted containers protect sensitive data at rest within container images and filesystems

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Use SBOMs to identify current deployments of vulnerable libraries, dependencies, and packages

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: CM-8
parts.prose: SBOMs serve as a machine-readable component inventory for identifying vulnerable dependencies

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Processes must execute only functions explicitly defined in an allow list

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: CM-2
parts.prose: Function allow-listing defines a baseline of permitted process execution

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: CM-7
parts.prose: Restricting processes to explicitly allowed functions enforces least functionality

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Functions are not be allowed to make changes to critical file system mount points

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: CM-5
parts.prose: Preventing function-level modifications to critical filesystem mount points is an access restriction for change

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Function access is only permitted to sanctioned services

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Either through networking restrictions or least privilege in permission models

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: AC-3
parts.prose: Restricting function access to sanctioned services enforces service-level access control

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Egress network connection is monitored to detect and prevent access to C&C (command and control) and other malicious network domains

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SI-4
parts.prose: Egress monitoring for command and control traffic detects compromised workload communication

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Ingress network inspection is employed detect and remove malicious payloads and commands

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For instance, SQL injection attacks can be detected using inspection.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SI-4
parts.prose: Ingress inspection for malicious payloads and commands is inbound network monitoring

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Serverless functions are run in tenant-based resource or performance isolation for similar data classifications

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: This may impact the performance due to limitations in the address space available to the isolation environment and should be considered for only the most sensitive workloads.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-7(21)
parts.prose: Tenant-based isolation of serverless functions by data classification implements component isolation

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Use a service mesh that eliminates implicit trust through data-in-motion protection (i.e. confidentiality, integrity, authentication, authorization)

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-7
parts.prose: Service mesh data-in-motion protection establishes boundary protection through confidentiality, integrity, and authentication

parts.name: overview
parts.prose: Guidelines for securing software deployments, including artifact verification, runtime policy enforcement, freshness validation, update management, logging, and incident response.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Trust confirmation verifies the image has a valid signature from an authorized source

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SR-4(3)
parts.prose: Image signature verification confirms the artifact is genuine and unaltered

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SR-4(4)
parts.prose: Validating the signature source traces the artifact back to an authorized origin

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Image runtime policies are enforced prior to deployment

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: CM-4
parts.prose: Pre-deployment policy enforcement gates image admission on integrity and trust criteria

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Image integrity and signature are verified prior to deployment

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SR-4(3)
parts.prose: Pre-deployment integrity verification confirms the image has not been altered

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SR-4(4)
parts.prose: Pre-deployment signature verification traces the image to its authorized build origin

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Applications provide logs regarding authentication, authorization, actions, and failures

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: AU-2
parts.prose: Authentication, authorization, action, and failure events are identified for application logging

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: AU-3
parts.prose: Application logs include authentication, authorization, action, and failure content

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Forensics capabilities are integrated into an incident response plan and procedures

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: AI, ML, or statistical modeling are used for behavioural and heuristic environment analysis to detect unwanted activities

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SI-3
parts.prose: AI/ML-based heuristic analysis extends malicious code detection beyond signature-based methods

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Clients can perform verification of artefacts and associated metadata

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SI-7
parts.prose: Client-side artifact verification confirms integrity before consumption

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Clients can verify the freshness of files

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Ensure clients can access latest versions and can verify if the provided files are out of date

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SI-7
parts.prose: Freshness verification detects stale or replayed artifacts

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A framework is used for managing software updates

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Consider using The Update Framework (TUF) to enforce the updating of software. TUF is a specification for delivering software updates in a secure, reliable and trusted way

parts.name: overview
parts.prose: Guidelines for secure software development practices including environment segregation, testing, code review, and CI server hardening.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A dedicated production environment is established

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Ensure that production workloads are in a separate, dedicated environment from non-production workloads. In the context of containers, this can mean separate clusters. In the case of VMs, separate networks.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SA-3(1)
parts.prose: A dedicated production environment implies managed separation from preproduction stages

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Dynamic deployments are leveraged for safer releases

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Blue/Green, Alpha/Beta, Canary, red-black deployments

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SA-8(31)
parts.prose: Dynamic deployment strategies (canary, blue-green, rolling) are secure system modification techniques

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Vulnerability and configuration scanning is integrated in the IDE or at the pull request

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SA-11(1)
parts.prose: IDE and pull request scanning shifts static analysis to the earliest point in the development lifecycle

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Dedicated development, testing, and production environments are established

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SA-15
parts.prose: Segregation of development, testing, and production environments is a development process standard

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Tests are built for business-critical code

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SA-11
parts.prose: Testing business-critical code is a developer evaluation activity

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Tests are built for business-critical infrastructure

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SA-11
parts.prose: Testing business-critical infrastructure is a developer evaluation activity

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Test suites are able to be run locally

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SA-11
parts.prose: Local test execution enables developer evaluation before code integration

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Test suites are available to run in a shared environment

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SA-11
parts.prose: Shared test environments enable collaborative developer evaluation

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Two non-author reviewers or approvers are required prior to merging

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SA-11(4)
parts.prose: Non-author code review is a manual evaluation gate prior to integration

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Code is clean and well commented

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Full infrastructure tests are used

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SA-11
parts.prose: Full infrastructure testing validates the complete deployment target

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Regression tests are used

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SA-11
parts.prose: Regression testing verifies existing functionality is preserved after changes

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Test suites are updated against new and emerging threats and developed into security regression tests

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SA-11
parts.prose: Security regression tests evolve developer evaluation against emerging threats

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A dedicated testing environment is established

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SA-3(1)
parts.prose: A dedicated testing environment is a managed preproduction stage in the development lifecycle

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Continuous integration server is isolated

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-39
parts.prose: CI server isolation prevents build processes from affecting or being affected by other workloads

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Threat model results are used to determine ROI for test development

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SA-11(2)
parts.prose: Threat model results inform test development priorities and investment decisions

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Secure configuration is implemented as the default state of the system

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Transitioning towards such a system involves making security a design requirement, inheriting default security configuration and supporting an exception process

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SA-8(23)
parts.prose: Secure default configuration implements the secure defaults engineering principle

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Integrate vulnerability and configuration scanning in both the IDE and at the CI system during pull request

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SA-11(1)
parts.prose: Integrating scanning in IDE and CI during pull request shifts static analysis left

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Implement at least one other non-author reviewer/approver prior to merging

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SA-11(4)
parts.prose: Requiring a non-author reviewer prior to merging is a manual code review gate

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Continuous integration server is isolated and hardened

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-39
parts.prose: CI server isolation and hardening prevents compromise of build infrastructure

parts.name: overview
parts.prose: Guidelines for secure distribution of container images, packages, and artifacts including signing, scanning, and registry security.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Trust is verified

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Artifacts ready for deployment are managed in a staging or pre-prod registry

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Container images are hardened following best practices

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Images contain least permissions to remain functional, do not allow for shell, do not include unnecessary libraries and dependencies, do not bind mount files in from the host, etc.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Static application security testing (SAST) is performed

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Static analysis is performed by dedicated SAST tools as well as linters

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Test suites follow the test pyramid

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Artifacts undergoing active development are held in a private registry

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Application manifests are scanned in CI pipeline

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: RA-5
parts.prose: Manifest scanning in CI detects vulnerabilities in declared dependencies before deployment

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: CI servers for sensitive workloads are isolated from other workloads

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-39

parts.name: overview
parts.prose: Guidelines for securing artefacts, including build process attestation, signing frameworks, key rotation, OCI registry support, and encryption.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Every step in the build process is signed and attested for process integrity

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The signing of artefacts should be performed at each stage of its life cycle. The final artefact bundle should include these collective signatures and itself be signed to give integrity to the completed artefact and all its associated metadata.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SI-1
parts.prose: Build process attestation establishes integrity policy for each pipeline stage

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SI-7
parts.prose: Signing each build step provides verifiable integrity of the build process

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Every step in the build process verifies previously generated signatures

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The integrity and provenance of images, deployment configuration, and application packages included in artefacts should all be validated using the signatures generated by each step in its build process to ensure compliance

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SI-1
parts.prose: Verifying signatures at each build step enforces integrity policy compliance

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SI-7
parts.prose: Signature verification at each stage detects unauthorized modification of build artifacts

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A framework is used to manage signing of artefacts

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Consider TUF/notary to sign OCI images. Notary makes use of a “root-of-trust” model to delegate trust from a single root to the individual teams or developers who sign artefacts. It uses additional metadata to allow clients to verify the freshness of content in a repository and protect against common attacks on update systems. Clients can make use of public keys to verify the contents of the repository.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: IA-5
parts.prose: The signing framework manages cryptographic authenticators for artifact identity

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A store is used to manage attestations

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Consider storing in-toto attestations in OCI registries alongside the image. Generated in-toto metadata needs to be stored and tracked for which a database or a dedicated store such as Grafeas can be used.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: AC-4(6)
parts.prose: Attestation metadata controls information flow decisions about artifact provenance

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Artefacts any given party is authorized to certify are limited

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Trust should not be granted universally or indefinitely. Artefacts or metadata that a given party is trusted to certify should be restricted using selective trust delegations. Trust must expire at predefined intervals, unless renewed as weel as a party must only be trusted to perform the tasks assigned to it to ensure compartmentatlization

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: AC-6
parts.prose: Limiting certification authority applies the principle of least privilege to artifact signing

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Rotation and revocation of private keys is supported

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The system must be prepared for when, not if, its private keys are compromised. The ability to rotate and revoke private keys must be built into the distribution mechanism. Additionally, multiple keys must be used for different tasks or roles, and a threshold of keys must be required for important roles. Finally, minimal trust must be placed in high-risk keys like those that are stored online or used in automated roles.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-12
parts.prose: Private key rotation and revocation are key management lifecycle activities

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A container registry that supports OCI image-spec images is used

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An internal image registry should be deployed and configured to support internal artefact distribution with the security properties described in this section.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Artefacts are encrypted before distribution and only authorized platforms have decryption capabilities

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Ensure contents of the artefact remain confidential in transit and at rest, until it is consumed. These artefacts can be encrypted so that they are accessible by authorized parties, such as the clusters, vulnerability scanners, etc. t is recommended organizations use key management and distribution systems with identity and attestation mechanisms (e.g. SPIFFE/SPIRE)

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: IA-5
parts.prose: Decryption capabilities are managed as platform authenticators

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-12
parts.prose: Encryption keys require lifecycle management

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-13
parts.prose: Artifact encryption uses approved cryptographic mechanisms

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-28(1)
parts.prose: Encrypted artifacts at rest use cryptographic protection

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-8
parts.prose: Encrypted distribution protects artifact confidentiality and integrity in transit

parts.name: overview
parts.prose: Guidelines for securing build pipelines, ensuring cryptographic guarantees, validation, and secure build environments.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Policy adherence is cryptographically guaranteed

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The presence and output of each build step should be attested during the build. The CNCF maintains the in-toto project that can be used to secure a chain of pipeline stages end-to-end with cryptographic guarantees. Build metadata should be evaluated against the policy template by using tools such as Open Policy Agent.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: CM-3(6)
parts.prose: Cryptographic guarantees of policy adherence provide tamper-evident configuration change control

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Environments and dependencies are validated before usage

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The build environment’s sources and dependencies must come from a secure, trusted source of truth. Checksums and any signatures should be validated both in the downloading or ingestion process, and again by the build worker. This should include validating package manager signatures, checking out specific Git commit hashes, and verifying SHA sums of input sources and binaries. After completing this validation, the downloading process should sign all binaries or libraries it is adding to the secure source

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: CM-3(2)
parts.prose: Validating environments and dependencies before usage tests configuration changes for impact

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Runtime security of build workers is validated

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Out-of-band verification of runtime environment security, as defined by execution of policies using tools such as seccomp, AppArmor, and SELinux, provides defense in depth against attacks on build infrastructure. High privilege kernel capabilities such as debugger, device, and network attachments should be restricted and monitored.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: CM-3(4)
parts.prose: Build worker runtime security validation is an automated security response to configuration changes

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Build artefacts are validated through verifiably reproducible builds

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A verifiably reproducible build is a build process where, given a source code commit hash and a set of build instructions, an end user should be able to reproduce the built artefact bit for bit.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: CM-3(4)
parts.prose: Reproducible builds provide automated verification of configuration change outcomes

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: External requirements from the build process are locked and verified

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: CM-3(2)
parts.prose: Locking and verifying external requirements tests configuration changes for impact before execution

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Sources of non-determinism are found and eliminated

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Reproducible-builds.org documents and offers solutions for many of these things. Diffoscope can be used to dig in and find the cause of differences when tracking down sources of non-determinism.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The build environment is recorded

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Ensure best practices outlined in cloud native security paper are followed to deploy a secure orchestration layer

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: CM-3(1)
parts.prose: Recording the build environment provides automated documentation of configuration changes

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Creation of the build environment is automated

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: CM-3(3)
parts.prose: Automated build environment creation implements automated change implementation mechanisms

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Builds are distributed across different infrastructure

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: CM-3(3)
parts.prose: Distributing builds across infrastructure uses automated change mechanisms to reduce single points of failure

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Build and related CI/CD steps are automated through a pipeline delivered as code

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SA-3
parts.prose: Pipeline-as-code defines the system development lifecycle for build automation

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Pipelines are standardized across projects

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A secured orchestration platform is provisioned to host the software factory

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Build workers are single use

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: AC-2
parts.prose: Single-use build workers enforce ephemeral account management for build processes

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Software factory has minimal network connectivity

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The software factory should have no network connectivity other than to connect to the trusted sources of hardened source code, the dependency repository and code signing infrastructure.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-7(3)
parts.prose: Minimal network connectivity for the software factory restricts access points as boundary protection

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Duties of each build worker are segregated

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: AC-5
parts.prose: Segregating build worker duties enforces separation of duties in the build pipeline

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Build worker environment and commands are passed in

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Inorder to limit hostile tooling and persistent impants from attackers, a Build Worker should start with a clean and isolated environmment. It should not be able to pull its own environment. Ensure environment variables and commands are explicitly passed to avoid any complicated and opaque build process

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: CM-2(2)
parts.prose: Passing in environment and commands enforces baseline configuration through automation

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Output is written to a separate secured storage repo

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The output artefact should be written to a separate shared storage from the inputs. A process separate from the Build Worker should then upload that artefact to an appropriate repository.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: AU-9(2)
parts.prose: Secured output storage protects build audit information in a separate repository

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Pipeline modification is only allowed through pipeline as code

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The pipeline configuration (pipeline as code) should be immutable and any modification shouldn't be possible. This prevents attackers from interacting and modifying the configuration. This model then requires appropriate authentication and authorization to be in place for the software and configuration of the pipeline

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: User roles are defined

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: AC-2
parts.prose: Defining user roles for the build pipeline is an account management activity

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Established practices are followed for establishing a root of trust from an offline source

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-17
parts.prose: Offline root of trust establishment aligns with PKI certificate management practices

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Short-lived workload certificates are used

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-23(5)
parts.prose: Short-lived workload certificates enforce session authenticity with time-bound validity

parts.name: overview
parts.prose: Guidelines for securing materials, including third-party artifact verification, SBOM generation, dependency tracking, vulnerability scanning, and software composition analysis.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Third party artefacts and open source libraries are verified

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All third party artefacts, open source libraries and any other dependencies should be verified as part of the continuous integration pipeline by validating their checksums against a known good source and validating any cryptographic signatures. Any software ingested must be scanned using Software Composition Analysis (SCA) and pentesting tools to detect whether any vulnerable open-source software is used in the final product.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SA-11
parts.prose: Verification of third-party artifacts is a supply chain evaluation activity

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: SBOM is required from third party suppliers

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Where possible, vendors should be required to provide Software Bills of Materials (SBOMs) containing the explicit details of the software and versions used within the supplied product as it provides a clear and direct link to the dependencies.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: CM-8
parts.prose: Third-party SBOMs provide component inventory for supply chain transparency

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Dependencies between open source components are tracked

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A register should be maintained of a project’s open source components, dependencies and vulnerabilities to help trace any deployed artefacts with new vulnerabilities. One of the most popular open source inventory implementations is OWASP Dependency-Track.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: CM-10
parts.prose: Tracking open source component dependencies enforces software usage restrictions

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Libraries are built based upon source code

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Trusted package managers and repositories are defined and prioritized

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Organizations should host their own package managers and artefact repositories, and restrict build machines to pull from only those sources.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An immutable SBOM of the code is generated

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There are currently two well known SBOM specifications: SPDX and CycloneDX

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Software is scanned for vulnerabilities

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: RA-5
parts.prose: Software vulnerability scanning identifies known weaknesses in third-party materials

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Software is scanned for license implications

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Licensing obligations must also be factored into the ingestion process. The Linux Foundation maintains the Open Compliance Program which hosts several tools to ensure released software meets legal and regulatory compliance requirements.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: CM-10
parts.prose: License compliance scanning enforces software usage restrictions for legal compliance

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Software composition analysis is run on ingested software

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The SCA tool will attempt to use heuristics to identify the direct and transitive dependencies, and can also serve as verification of SBOM content. This data will then be matched against data from a number of data feeds containing vulnerability data to highlight any vulnerabilities in the dependent packages.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SA-11(1)
parts.prose: SCA combines static analysis to evaluate ingested software

parts.name: overview
parts.prose: Guidelines for securing the source code, including commit signing, branch protection, secret prevention, access control, MFA enforcement, and automated security scanning.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Commits and tags are signed

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: GPG keys or S/MIME certificates are used to sign the source code

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SI-7
parts.prose: Signed commits and tags establish integrity and authorship of source code changes

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Full attestation and verification is enforced for protected branches

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Branch protection is enabled on the mainline and release branches with force push disabled

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: AC-6(3)
parts.prose: Attestation enforcement for protected branches restricts code modification to authorized privileged commands

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Secrets are not committed to the source code repository unless encrypted

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Implement tooling to detect secrets or to prevent certain files from being pushed which may contain plaintext sensitive materials, such as via a .gitignore and/or .gitattributes file, client-side hook (pre-commit), server-side hook (pre-receive or update), and/or as a step in the CI process

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-12(3)
parts.prose: Encrypting secrets before repository commit requires asymmetric key infrastructure

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Individuals or teams with write access to a repository are defined

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Implement codeowners (or equivalent)

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: PL-1
parts.prose: Defining repository write access is an access planning and policy activity

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Software security scanning and testing is automated

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Security specific scans should be performed, including Static Application Security Tests (SAST) and Dynamic Application Security Tests (DAST). Both the coverage and results of these tests should be published as part of the repository information to help downstream consumers of software better assess the stability, reliability, and/or suitability of a product or library.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: RA-5
parts.prose: Automation of security scanning ensures consistent vulnerability detection in source code

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Contribution policies are established and adhered to

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Define configuration options or configuration rules witthin SCM platforms allow repository administrators to enforce security, hygiene and operational policies.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: PL-1
parts.prose: Contribution policies establish governance procedures for source code changes

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Roles are defined and aligned to functional responsibilities

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Define roles by using principle of least privileges to provide access based on function such as Developer, Maintainer, Owner, Reviewer, Approver, and Guest

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: PL-1
parts.prose: Defining roles aligned to functional responsibilities is a planning and policy activity

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An independent four-eyes principle is enforced

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The author(s) of a request may not also be the approver of the request. At least two reviewers with equal or greater expertise should review & approve the request.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SA-11
parts.prose: The four-eyes principle ensures independent evaluation of code changes

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Branch protection rules are used

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: SCM platforms allow the configuration and restriction of source code operations on individual branches. Protection rules can be used to enforce the usage of pull requests with specified precondition and approval rules, ensuring that a human code review process is followed or an automated status checking of a branch occurs. Additionally, protected branches can be used to disallow dangerous use of force pushes, preventing the overwrite of commit histories and potential obfuscation of code changes.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SA-8
parts.prose: Branch protection rules implement security engineering principles for source code governance

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: MFA is enforced for accessing source code repositories

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: IA-2(1)
parts.prose: Repository MFA enforcement requires multi-factor authentication for organizational users accessing source code

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: SSH keys are used to provide developers access to source code repositories

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: AC-1
parts.prose: SSH key-based access to repositories implements access control procedures for developer authentication

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A key rotation policy is maintained

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: It is recommended to implement a key rotation policy to ensure that compromised keys will cease to be usable after a certain period of time. When a private key is known to have been compromised, it should be revoked and replaced immediately to shut off access for any unauthorized user. Organizations may also consider using short lived certificates or keys, which reduces the reliance on certificate revocation systems.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: AC-2(1)
parts.prose: Key rotation policy defines prerequisites for automated credential management

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Short-lived or ephemeral credentials are used for machine and service access

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Short-life credential issuance encourages the use of fine grained permissions and automation in provisioning access tokens. For CI/CD pipeline agents, short-lived access tokens should be considered instead of password-based credentials. The use of very short-lived tokens like OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, etc., will help to implement more secure access and increase the security assurance.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: AC-2(1)
parts.prose: Ephemeral credentials automate credential lifecycle management for machine and service accounts

parts.name: overview
parts.prose: Guidelines for security assurance, including network policies, incident response, platform hardening, threat modeling, identity management, and GitOps security practices.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Network policies enforce east-west network communication within the container deployment is limited to only that which is authorized for access

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: AC-6(3)
parts.prose: East-west network policies restrict lateral communication to authorized network-level privileged commands

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Incident response considers cloud native workloads

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: workloads which may not always conform with some underlying assumptions about node isolation (new pod instances could run on a different server), networking (e.g. IP addresses are assigned dynamically) and immutability (e.g. runtime changes to container are not persisted across restarts)

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: CA-7
parts.prose: Cloud native incident response requires continuous monitoring of workload behavior

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: IR-4
parts.prose: Incident handling processes must account for cloud native workload dynamics

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: IR-4(5)
parts.prose: Automated disabling of compromised cloud native workloads

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Incident response accounts for appropriate evidence handling and collection of cloud native workloads

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: IR-5(1)
parts.prose: Evidence handling and collection for cloud native workloads requires automated tracking and data collection

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Rootless builds are employed

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Cgroups and system groups are used to isolate workloads and deployments

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: MAC implementations are employed

parts.name: guidance

parts.name: overview
parts.prose: Guidelines for securing storage, including encryption at rest, data availability, integrity validation, namespace boundaries, access policies, and artifact registry management.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Storage control plane management interface requires mutual authentication and TLS for connections

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SC-8
parts.prose: Mutual authentication and TLS for control plane connections protects transmission confidentiality and integrity

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Data availability is achieved through parity or mirroring, erasure coding or replicas

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SI-13
parts.prose: Parity, mirroring, and replicas are predictable failure prevention mechanisms for data availability

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Hashing and checksums are added to blocks, objects or files

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: primarily designed to detect and recover from corrupted data, but can also add a layer of protection against the tampering of data.

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: CM-7
parts.prose: Checksums constrain storage to validated data, supporting least functionality

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SI-7
parts.prose: Hashing and checksums verify data integrity

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Data backup storage locations employ like access controls and security policies to that of the data storage source

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: SA-9

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Secure erasure adhering to OPAL standards is employed for returned or non-functional devices

parts.title: CP-9

parts.name: mapping-rationale
parts.title: MP-6

parts.name: statement

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The encryption may be implemented in the storage client or storage server and granularity of the encryption will vary by system (e.g. per volume, per group or global keys)

parts.name: mapping-rationale

parts.name: statement
